item.title: BridgeBio Stands Tall as Phase 3 Data Put Dwarfism Drug on Track for FDA Filing
item.description: Infigratinib achieved statistically significant improvement in growth rate and body composition in a Phase 3 clinical trial that tested the BridgeBio Pharma drug in achondroplasia, the most common form of dwarfism. item.description: Mayo Clinic has about 100 petabytes of structured and unstructured EHR data, and about 28 petabytes have been de-identified, but in the Mayo Clinic way. item.title: Closing the CKD Care Gap with Value-Based Care Models
item.description: VBC models deliver significant benefits for CKD management by coordinating medical, behavioral, and social support through multidisciplinary teams. This approach enables providers to personalize care, address barriers to access, and use data-driven strategies to identify and prioritize high-risk patients. item.title: PTC Therapeutics Ends Bid to Seek FDA Approval for Rare Muscle Disease Drug
item.description: PTC Therapeutics said it cannot resolve differences it has with the FDA in interpreting clinical trial data for Translarna, a drug it developed for Duchenne muscular dystrophy. The rare disease drug developer’s decision to withdraw Translarna’s FDA submission comes nearly a year after a negative European regulatory decision for the drug. item.title: Disc Medicine Rare Disease Drug Picked for Faster Regulatory Review Is Rejected by the FDA
item.description: The FDA asked for more data to determine whether Disc Medicine’s bitopertin is benefiting patients with erythropoietic protoporphyria, a rare blood disorder. Analysts say it’s a surprising delay considering bitopertin is one of the first drugs in a new FDA pilot program that speeds up regulatory review of medicines deemed critical for national security or public health.
